stem: Which statement best describes valid informed consent for a proposed procedure?

options.A: A signature alone is sufficient even if the procedure has not been explained
options.B: The patient receives adequate information about the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives and voluntarily decides while able to make the decision
options.C: Consent is most valid when obtained after sedation so the patient is less anxious
options.D: A family member should sign whenever one is available, even if the patient has decision-making capacity

rationale: CMS requires hospital informed-consent processes to contain information that allows patients or their representatives to make fully informed decisions about care. HHS policy analysis describes informed consent in terms of adequate disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternatives and the core elements of being informed, voluntary, and competent. A signature alone does not create valid informed consent, and a capable patient ordinarily makes the decision personally.
educational_objective: Recognize informed consent as an informed, voluntary decision by a patient with decision-making capacity rather than merely obtaining a signature.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
source_document_title: QSO-24-10-Hospitals: Revisions and Clarifications to Hospital Interpretive Guidelines for Informed Consent; Advance Directives and Advance Care Planning: Legal and Policy Issues
source_version_date: CMS QSO-24-10-Hospitals issued 2024-04-01; HHS ASPE legal/policy review published 2007
source_locator: CMS QSO-24-10-Hospitals > informed consent policies/forms and fully informed decisions; HHS ASPE 2007 > Informed Consent > disclosure, voluntariness, competence
source_claim_supported: Hospital consent processes must support fully informed decisions; informed consent includes adequate disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternatives and an informed, voluntary decision by a competent decision-maker.
correction_summary: Final reaudit retained the valid informed-consent elements and corrected source chronology so the older HHS ASPE legal/policy review is not misrepresented as a newly updated publication.
audit_findings: B incorporates disclosure, voluntariness, and decision-making ability. A reduces consent to documentation only; C undermines capacity and timing; D improperly substitutes a family member for a capable patient. No second answer remains.
